# nish/net/http3

The server side of an HTTP/3 connection (RFC 9114) on the streams of a `QuicConnection` (`nish/net/quic`): the control stream and SETTINGS both ways, the QPACK encoder and decoder streams (opened, at dynamic table capacity 0), requests and responses on bidirectional streams with their bodies streamed both ways, GOAWAY, and RFC 9114's error codes. Field sections are encoded and decoded by `nish/net/qpack` and checked by `nish/net/http-fields`.

```ts
import {
  H3_AGAIN,
  H3_ALPN,
  H3_CLOSED,
  H3_CONTROL_FRAME_MAX,
  H3_DATA,
  H3_DROPPED,
  H3_END,
  H3_ERROR,
  H3_GOAWAY,
  H3_INVALID,
  H3_MAX_SESSIONS,
  H3_NEED_MORE,
  H3_NO_APPLICATION_PROTOCOL,
  H3_REQUEST,
  H3_RESET,
  H3_STOPPED,
  H3_STREAM,
  H3_TOO_LARGE,
  H3_TRAILERS,
  H3_WRITABLE,
  Http3Config,
  Http3Connection,
} from "nish/net/http3";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { Http3Config, Http3Connection, H3_NEED_MORE, H3_ERROR, H3_END } from "nish/net/http3";
import { httpFieldBytes } from "nish/net/http-fields";
import { QuicConnection } from "nish/net/quic";

// Once per slot, beside a server QuicConnection; restart() per connection.
function open(quic: QuicConnection): Http3Connection {
  return new Http3Connection(new Http3Config(), quic);
}

// After each quic.receive(...):
function serve(h3: Http3Connection): void {
  const names: u8[][] = [httpFieldBytes("content-type")];
  const values: u8[][] = [httpFieldBytes("text/plain")];
  const body: u8[] = httpFieldBytes("hello\n");
  let event: i32 = h3.next();
  while (event !== H3_NEED_MORE && event !== H3_ERROR) {
    // H3_REQUEST: h3.stream, h3.fields (method, path, get("accept"))
    // H3_DATA: h3.data[h3.dataStart .. h3.dataStart + h3.dataLength)
    if (event === H3_END) {   // the request is whole: respond
      h3.respond(h3.stream, 200, names, values, false);
      h3.writeData(h3.stream, body, 0, toI32(body.length), true);   // answers how much it took
    }
    event = h3.next();
  }
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="Http3​Config" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#http3config">

The connection's caps, fixed when it is made.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Http3​Connection" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#http3connection">

<scalar-callout type="info">

It is sans-IO in the way the QUIC connection under it is: the carrier
hands the `QuicConnection` its datagrams and takes the ones it sends, and
this module reads and writes that connection's streams. `nish/net/http3-server`
runs it over a UDP socket with ALPN `h3`.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Events">

`next()` reads the streams the QUIC connection has news for and answers the
first thing that means something to the program:
- `H3_REQUEST` (a request's field section, in `fields`),
- `H3_DATA` (a piece of its body, a window onto `data` valid until the next
call),
- `H3_TRAILERS`,
- `H3_END` (the request ended, and its `content-length`, if any, matched),
- `H3_RESET` (the stream is gone: the client reset it or stopped it, or it
broke a rule that resets it — `errorCode` says which, `resetByPeer` who),
- `H3_WRITABLE` (a stream whose write was held back can take more),
- `H3_GOAWAY` (the client is going away; `lastStreamId` is its push ID),
- and `H3_ERROR`, final: the connection broke a rule, it is closed with
`errorCode`, and every later call answers it again.

`H3_NEED_MORE` asks for more datagrams. A request's events come in order —
REQUEST, DATA…, TRAILERS, END — and after `H3_RESET` its stream has no more.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Back-pressure">

**Back-pressure** is QUIC's flow control. A body is read only as the
program calls `next()`, `bodyChunk` bytes at most at a time, and QUIC gives
the client more credit only as its receive buffer is read. `writeData`
takes as much as the stream's send buffer has room for and answers how much;
when it took less, `H3_WRITABLE` names the stream once acknowledgements free
room. HEADERS and trailers go whole or not at all (`H3_AGAIN`).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="ALPN">

A QUIC connection whose handshake chose anything but `h3` is
closed with CRYPTO_ERROR no_application_protocol (0x0178) on the first
`next()` after it connects, before any HTTP/3 byte (§3.1).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Streams">

**Streams** (§6). The connection opens its control stream, sends SETTINGS
first on it (SETTINGS_QPACK_MAX_TABLE_CAPACITY 0, SETTINGS_QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS
0 and SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE), and opens its QPACK encoder and
decoder streams, on which it sends nothing but their types. The client's
encoder and decoder streams go to `nish/net/qpack`'s capacity-0 handling.
A unidirectional stream of a type it does not know is asked to stop
(H3_STREAM_CREATION_ERROR) and read to its end (§6.2).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**What it refuses.**

A connection error closes the QUIC connection with the code:
- a second control, encoder or decoder stream, or a push stream from a client
(H3_STREAM_CREATION_ERROR, §6.2.1, §6.2.2);
- a control stream whose first frame is not SETTINGS (H3_MISSING_SETTINGS);
- the end, reset or STOP_SENDING of any critical stream, either side's
(H3_CLOSED_CRITICAL_STREAM);
- a frame where it may not be — DATA or HEADERS on the control stream, a
control frame on a request stream, a second SETTINGS, DATA before HEADERS,
anything but the end after trailers, any PUSH_PROMISE from a client, and an
HTTP/2 type HTTP/3 reserves (H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED, §7.2.8);
- a frame cut off by its stream's end or a payload of the wrong length
(H3_FRAME_ERROR, §7.1);
- a SETTINGS frame `nish/net/http3-frame` refuses (H3_SETTINGS_ERROR);
- a GOAWAY whose push ID rose, a MAX_PUSH_ID that fell, a CANCEL_PUSH past
the push IDs allowed (H3_ID_ERROR, §5.2, §7.2.7, §7.2.3);
- a control frame past `H3_CONTROL_FRAME_MAX` (H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD);
- and QPACK's three.

A stream error resets one request, both ways, and the connection lives: a
field section `nish/net/http-fields` refuses, and a body that disagrees with
`content-length` (H3_MESSAGE_ERROR, §4.1.2); a request stream that ends
before its HEADERS (H3_REQUEST_INCOMPLETE, §4.1.1); a request on a stream at
or past the ID of the GOAWAY this side sent (H3_REQUEST_REJECTED, §5.2). A
request whose field section is longer than `maxFieldSectionSize` — the frame,
or the section once decoded — is answered with a 431, never reaches the
program, and its stream is asked to stop with H3_NO_ERROR (§4.2.2, §4.1.2).

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="No server push">

It never sends PUSH_PROMISE; a client's MAX_PUSH_ID is
allowed, checked and ignored.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Caps are start-up numbers**, all in `Http3Config`. The stream state for
every QUIC stream slot and the control frame are made by the constructor;
the body chunk and the field section are borrowed, around one read, from
pools that a server's connections share and that a standalone
connection keeps one buffer each of. A field section's
names and values are copied into arrays the connection keeps, which grow to
the largest section seen and are then reused, so a warm connection
allocates nothing per request (`docs/security/http3.md`, H3-2). A peer's
counters saturate, and the lookup of a stream's state is the QUIC
connection's own hash index (`QuicStreams.slotOf`), never a scan.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Extended CONNECT and WebTransport">

With `extendedConnect` the connection
sends SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL 1 and a request may carry `:protocol`
(RFC 9220); without it `:protocol` is malformed, H3_MESSAGE_ERROR.

`webtransportSessions` above 0 turns that on and also sends
SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM 1, draft-02's SETTINGS_ENABLE_WEBTRANSPORT 1 and
draft-07's SETTINGS_WEBTRANSPORT_MAX_SESSIONS, and `nish/net/webtransport`
runs its sessions on top: a request then waits for the client's SETTINGS
(draft-02 §3.1), and a stream that opens with WebTransport's unidirectional
type (0x54) or bidirectional signal (0x41) is read as far as its session ID,
held unread and named in `H3_STREAM` until the program calls `acceptStream`
(its bytes then come as H3_DATA, H3_END, H3_RESET and H3_STOPPED, and
`writeStream` writes them as they are) or `refuseStream`.

`openStream` opens one of this side's; `writeDataWhole` writes a capsule; a
GOAWAY still lets a session's new stream in, and `H3_DROPPED` names a request
stream that ended before its request reached the program. The client's
SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL and SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM must be 0 or 1
(H3_SETTINGS_ERROR), a session ID that is no client-initiated bidirectional
stream is H3_ID_ERROR, and the signal anywhere but a stream's start is
H3_FRAME_ERROR. Holding every request, not only an extended CONNECT, until
the client's SETTINGS keeps a decoded field section from having to be held
per stream; it costs a request only when the client's control stream is lost
or reordered.

</scalar-detail>

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

<scalar-detail title="The Date">

A response carries the `date` in `conn.date`, 29 bytes of
IMF-fixdate, right after `:status`, unless the program's fields hold their
own; trailers carry none. It counts against the peer's
SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE. A bare connection has no clock, so `date`
starts empty and nothing is sent; `Http3Server` fills it from its
`HttpDate` (RFC 9110 §6.6.1).

</scalar-detail>

Written from RFC 9114 and RFC 9204, not ported from another implementation.

## Classes

### Http3Config

The connection's caps, fixed when it is made. `maxFieldSectionSize` is
advertised in SETTINGS and is the largest HEADERS frame read and the
largest section decoded; `bodyChunk` the most body handed to the program at
once; `writeChunk` the largest DATA frame written.

```ts
class Http3Config
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http3Config()` |  |
| `bodyChunk: i32` | The body buffer: the largest `H3_DATA` window. |
| `extendedConnect: boolean` | Whether `:protocol` is accepted (RFC 9220's extended CONNECT), and SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL sent. WebTransport turns it on. |
| `headTimeout: i32` | The milliseconds a request's head may take to arrive whole, from its first byte or the last head before it, before `clock` closes the connection with H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD (H3-5), 1 to 2^31 - 1. A body that trickles after its head is the program's to time, as a long response is. |
| `idleTimeout: i32` | The milliseconds a connection may go without progress while no request is in hand before `clock` closes it (H3-5), 1 to 2^31 - 1. Progress is the connection starting, a request's head arriving whole, and the last request in hand finishing. With no request open the close is H3_NO_ERROR; with one still short of its head it is H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD. |
| `maxFieldSectionSize: i32` | SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE (§4.2.2): past it a request is answered with a 431. |
| `webtransportSessions: i32` | The WebTransport sessions this side takes at once (`nish/net/webtransport`), 0 for none. Above 0 it turns on extended CONNECT and sends SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM, SETTINGS_ENABLE_WEBTRANSPORT and SETTINGS_WEBTRANSPORT_MAX_SESSIONS, and the QUIC connection must take DATAGRAM frames; at 0 it must not (RFC 9297 §2.1.1). |
| `writeChunk: i32` | The largest DATA frame `writeData` starts. |

### Http3Connection

One HTTP/3 connection, server side, over `quic`. The fields after the
buffers are the last event's; the module comment says which event sets
which.

```ts
class Http3Connection
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http3Connection(config: Http3Config, quic: QuicConnection)` | A connection under `config` over `quic`, whose configuration must let a HEADERS frame of `maxFieldSectionSize` fit half a stream's buffer, and one on every request stream fit half the connection's window, and let the client open the three unidirectional streams it needs and this side open its own three (§6.2). A cap out of range panics. |
| `data: u8[]` | H3_DATA's bytes, and where a payload being skipped is read to: a `bodyChunk`-byte buffer borrowed from `dataPool` for the read that needs it and held while an H3_DATA window is live, else an empty array. Any event but H3_DATA gives the buffer back, zeroed as far as reads wrote. |
| `dataLength: i32` | H3_DATA's window length in bytes, 1 to `bodyChunk`; valid until the next `next()`. |
| `dataPool: BufferPool` | Where `data` is borrowed from: the connection's own pool until its server lends it the server's. |
| `dataStart: i32` | Where H3_DATA's window onto `data` starts. |
| `date: u8[]` | The `date` every response carries (RFC 9110 §6.6.1), as the 29 bytes of an IMF-fixdate, or empty for none. A bare connection has no clock, so it starts empty; `Http3Server` points it at its `HttpDate`'s bytes, which that rewrites in place once a second. |
| `decoder: QpackDecoder` | The QPACK decoder of the client's field sections, at dynamic table capacity 0; it also reads the client's encoder stream. |
| `encoder: QpackEncoder` | The QPACK encoder of this side's field sections; it also reads the client's decoder stream. |
| `errorCode: i64` | H3_RESET's, H3_STOPPED's and H3_ERROR's code. |
| `fields: HttpFields` | The last request's or trailers' fields, valid until the next of either. |
| `generation: i32` | How many times `restart` ran: a layer above that keeps state per connection compares it to know when to forget its own. |
| `lastStreamId: i64` | H3_GOAWAY's push ID. |
| `live: i32` | Requests open, taken and not yet finished both ways, plus the bidirectional WebTransport streams held after this side's GOAWAY for a session below it. |
| `maxPushId: i64` | The client's MAX_PUSH_ID, or -1 until it sends one. It is checked (it may not fall, and bounds CANCEL_PUSH) and otherwise unused, since this side never pushes. |
| `peer: Http3Settings` | The client's SETTINGS. |
| `peerControl: i64` | The ID of the client's control stream, or -1 until its stream type has been read. |
| `peerDecoder: i64` | The ID of the client's QPACK decoder stream, or -1 until its stream type has been read. |
| `peerEncoder: i64` | The ID of the client's QPACK encoder stream, or -1 until its stream type has been read. |
| `quic: QuicConnection` | The QUIC connection this one runs on, given to the constructor and kept for its life. |
| `rejected: i32` | Counters for a log or a test, each saturating and zeroed by `restart`. This one: request streams refused because their ID is at or past the one this side's GOAWAY named, and WebTransport streams dropped because their session's is. |
| `resetByPeer: boolean` | Whether H3_RESET came from the client. |
| `sectionPool: BufferPool` | Where the buffer a HEADERS payload is read into whole, for the decoder, is borrowed from around one read and decode: the connection's own pool until its server lends it the server's. |
| `session: i64` | H3_STREAM's session ID. |
| `settingIds: i64[]` | The identifiers of the SETTINGS this side sends, in the order sent; fixed by the constructor. |
| `settingsSeen: boolean` | Whether the client's SETTINGS have arrived. |
| `state: i32` | 0 while the connection is open; 1 once it failed (H3_ERROR), which only `restart` undoes. |
| `stream: i64` | The last event's stream. |
| `streamErrors: i32` | Requests reset for breaking a rule (a stream error, §8): a malformed message, a body that disagrees with `content-length`, a stream that ends before its HEADERS, a trailer section too large. |
| `tooLarge: i32` | Requests whose field section was past `maxFieldSectionSize`: answered with a 431, or reset when the 431 did not fit. |
| `webtransport: boolean` | Whether WebTransport is on: `webtransportSessions` above 0. Fixed by the constructor. |
| `acceptStream(id: i64): i32` | Lets a stream H3_STREAM held go: its bytes come as H3_DATA from the next `next()`, and the program may write it. Answers 0, or H3_CLOSED for a stream that is not one held. |
| `awaitsRequest(id: i64): boolean` | Whether request stream `id` has not yet had its field section read: not opened, opened by a later stream's frame (RFC 9000 §3.2), or still waiting for its HEADERS. A WebTransport stream that names it as its session may wait for it. |
| `clock(now: i64): i64` | Runs the connection's clock (H3-5): closes the QUIC connection once it has gone `idleTimeout` without progress while no request is in hand, or a request's head has waited `headTimeout`, and otherwise answers when to look again. `Http3Server` calls it on every flush of the slot; a program driving a connection itself calls it after each `next` and when the time it answered comes. It allocates nothing. The clock starts with HTTP/3, on the first `next` after the handshake chose `h3`: a connection the program runs another protocol on, and never asks for an event, is left to QUIC's own idle timeout. |
| `discardRequest(id: i64, code: i64): i32` | Stops reading request stream `id`: the client is asked to stop with `code` and what it still sends is dropped unseen, whether or not this side has finished its response — a refused WebTransport session's stream, after its status. Answers 0, or H3_CLOSED for a stream that is not a request here. |
| `goaway(): i32` | Sends GOAWAY (§5.2): the client's requests on streams below the ID it names — every stream the client has opened so far — are processed, and any it opens from there on is refused with H3_REQUEST_REJECTED. A second call never raises the ID, and sends nothing when the ID has not fallen. Answers 0, or H3_AGAIN before this side's control stream is open or while it has no room for the frame. |
| `isDone(): boolean` | Whether this side sent GOAWAY and every request it took has finished both ways, every byte of each response acknowledged: the carrier may close the connection. |
| `next(): i32` | Reads what the QUIC connection has for the program and answers the next event (see the module comment). Call it after every datagram the QUIC connection takes, until it answers H3_NEED_MORE or H3_ERROR. |
| `openStream(session: i64, bidirectional: boolean): i64` | Opens a WebTransport stream of this side's for `session` (draft-02 §4.1, §4.2): unidirectional with the type 0x54, or bidirectional with the signal 0x41, and the session ID, which go before anything written. Answers its ID, H3_AGAIN while the client's MAX_STREAMS allows no more, or H3_CLOSED with WebTransport off or the connection failed. |
| `refuseStream(id: i64, code: i64): i32` | Refuses WebTransport stream `id` with `code`: its side here is reset, the client's asked to stop, and what it sent read and dropped. Answers 0, or H3_CLOSED for a stream that is not a WebTransport one. |
| `reset(id: i64, code: i64): i32` | Resets request stream `id` both ways with `code` — H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED, or H3_REQUEST_REJECTED for one the program did not process (§4.1.1). Answers 0 or H3_CLOSED. |
| `resetStream(id: i64, code: i64): i32` | Resets this side of WebTransport stream `id` with `code`; the client's side goes on. |
| `respond(id: i64, status: i32, names: u8[][], values: u8[][], endStream: boolean): i32` | Sends the response head on request stream `id`: `status` (200 to 599) and the fields `names`/`values` (lowercase names, no pseudo-headers), ending the stream when `endStream`. Answers 0; H3_CLOSED for a stream that is not an open request; H3_INVALID for a second head, a status out of range or a field `httpFieldsCheckOutgoing` refuses; H3_TOO_LARGE for a section past the client's SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE; or H3_AGAIN. |
| `restart(): void` | Puts the connection back as the constructor left it, for the QUIC connection's next peer (call it after `quic.reset`): no stream known, QPACK's state and the client's SETTINGS forgotten, and any buffer still borrowed given back. It allocates nothing. |
| `stopStream(id: i64, code: i64): i32` | Asks the client to stop its side of WebTransport stream `id` with `code`, and drops what it still sends; this side's goes on. Answers 0 or H3_CLOSED. |
| `writeData(id: i64, buf: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, endStream: boolean): i32` | Writes up to `len` bytes of `buf` from `off` as the response body of stream `id`, in DATA frames of at most `writeChunk`, and ends the stream when `endStream` and every byte was taken. Answers how many bytes it took — fewer than `len` only when the send buffer filled, and H3_WRITABLE then names the stream once it has room — or H3_AGAIN when it took none; H3_CLOSED, or H3_INVALID before the head or when `endStream` would cut short the DATA frame the last call started. A window outside `buf` panics. |
| `writeDataWhole(id: i64, buf: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, fin: boolean): i32` | Writes `buf[off .. off + len)` as one DATA frame on request stream `id`, whole or not at all, with the FIN when `fin`: a capsule (RFC 9297 §3.2) goes this way, so the client never reads half of one. Answers 0; H3_AGAIN while the send buffer lacks room, and H3_WRITABLE then names the stream; or as `writeData` refuses, and H3_TOO_LARGE for a frame past the stream's buffer. A window outside `buf` panics. |
| `writeStream(id: i64, buf: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, fin: boolean): i32` | Writes up to `len` bytes of `buf` from `off` to WebTransport stream `id`, as they are, and its FIN when `fin` and every byte was taken. Answers how many it took — fewer only when the send buffer filled, and H3_WRITABLE then names the stream — or H3_AGAIN when it took none, or H3_CLOSED for a stream with no side here to write, finished, reset, held or stopped. A window outside `buf` panics. |
| `writeTrailers(id: i64, names: u8[][], values: u8[][]): i32` | Writes a trailer section on request stream `id` after its body, which ends the stream. Answers as `respond` does; H3_INVALID before the head or inside a DATA frame `writeData` has not finished. |

The ALPN protocol identifier of HTTP/3 (RFC 9114 §3.1).

<scalar-card title="-32" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_CLOSED: i32`

A write to a stream that is not an open request: Linux's EPIPE.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_DATA: i32`

Request body bytes: `stream`, `data[dataStart .. dataStart + dataLength)`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_DROPPED: i32`

A request stream ended before its request reached the program (only with
`webtransportSessions` on): `stream`. Nothing is owed the program; a
WebTransport layer lets go of the streams that waited for it as a session.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_END: i32`

The request ended whole: `stream`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_ERROR: i32`

The connection failed with `errorCode` and is closed. Final.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_GOAWAY: i32`

The client sent GOAWAY: `lastStreamId`, its push ID.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-22" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_INVALID: i32`

A write of fields or a status the program may not send, or out of order: Linux's EINVAL.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_NEED_MORE: i32`

`next` has nothing more until more datagrams arrive.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0178" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_NO_APPLICATION_PROTOCOL: i64`

CRYPTO_ERROR with TLS's no_application_protocol alert (RFC 9001 §4.8): a handshake that did not choose `h3`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_REQUEST: i32`

A request's field section: `stream`, `fields`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_RESET: i32`

The stream is gone: `stream`, `errorCode`, `resetByPeer`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_STOPPED: i32`

The client sent STOP_SENDING for a WebTransport stream this side writes, and QUIC reset it: `stream`, `errorCode`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_STREAM: i32`

A WebTransport stream arrived (only with `webtransportSessions` on):
`stream`, and `session`, the session ID its first bytes named. It is held,
unread, until the program calls `acceptStream` or `refuseStream`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-90" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_TOO_LARGE: i32`

A field section past what the client takes, or past a stream's buffer: Linux's EMSGSIZE.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_TRAILERS: i32`

A trailer section: `stream`, `fields`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H3_WRITABLE: i32`

A stream whose write was held back can take more: `stream`.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
